unit: one (case, vendor) pair — case = a distinct idea, vendor = the covered_by name a parity judge stamped for it. Arm and rep are STRIPPED from the export, so a label cannot be tuned toward an arm; the same vendor stamped by two arms is one pair with one label.
criterion: FROZEN in probes/parity_eval_harness.py's docstring before the first judge call. yes = the named entity is a REAL, currently-available product, first-party platform feature, or (for a `substitute` stamp) a concrete free/DIY route, AND it delivers this idea's CORE MECHANISM for this idea's buyer, outright or in substantial part. no = (i) not a product at all (content page, blog post, listicle, buyer's guide, directory, forum thread, retailer/marketplace SKU page, PDF checklist); (ii) a real product doing a DIFFERENT job than the idea's core mechanism; (iii) not identifiable as a specific named vendor. unclear = evidence too thin to decide. BORDERLINES RESOLVE TO `no` — the harm being measured is a false positive that caps a novel idea's market_fit, so an unproven vendor must not be credited as a genuine incumbent. Class correctness (shipped vs partial vs substitute) is NOT part of this label.
application_notes: Decided from the idea's value_proposition + technical_approach, the judge's own evidence line, and the recorded Serper snippet the stamp was drawn from — i.e. the evidence the pipeline actually had. World knowledge is used only to decide whether the named entity is a real product, never to supply a mechanism match the evidence does not show.

AMBIGUITY THE CRITERION LEFT OPEN, resolved uniformly and blind to arm: if the named entity cannot be resolved to a specific product/vendor/URL in the snippet, then a `shipped`/`partial` stamp (which asserts a COMMERCIAL product) is `no`, and a `substitute` stamp (where a generic free/DIY route is legitimate) is `unclear`.

SAME-BUYER REQUIREMENT is applied strictly: a product that ships the mechanism for a DIFFERENT payer (e.g. a city-government compliance suite vs the idea's short-term-rental host) is `no`. This makes the absolute precision level conservative for EVERY arm; between-arm contrasts are unaffected because the rule is applied identically.

`world` is an AUXILIARY field, not the label: it records whether the vendor is a genuine incumbent for this mechanism under an evidence-independent reading (world knowledge allowed). It exists so the 'right vendor, unauditable evidence line' class is countable instead of hidden inside `no`. Headline precision uses `label`.

Evidence-grounding rule for a stamp whose evidence line is ABSENT from every recorded snippet (the `vendor_in_snippets` flag): `unclear` when the named entity is a real product plausibly doing this job, `no` when the entity or the job is wrong. World knowledge never supplies a mechanism match the evidence does not show.
